events.what: 321-point three-distance configuration in R^63 proving b(63) >= 65, lowering the smallest known counterexample dimension from 64 to 63; produced by Grinsztajn with GPT-5.5 Pro, independently found by Konz and by Ji
events.ai_basis: Wikipedia's AI-discoveries list credits Max Grinsztajn, prompting GPT-5.5 Pro; Ji's independent reproduction: 'The example and proof were generated entirely by ChatGPT using GPT 5.6 Sol.'

events.what: Ji's arXiv:2608.12561 writeup of the same dimension-63 construction, withdrawn two days later over priority
events.credibility_reason: Withdrawn (for priority, not error); duplicates the Grinsztajn event, which carries the result
events.ai_basis: The example and proof were generated entirely by ChatGPT using GPT 5.6 Sol.

events.what: Tolmachev and Voronov lower the upper bound on the Borsuk number in R^4 from 9 to 8

judgement.doubts: Grinsztajn's May 2026 priority and GPT-5.5 Pro attribution rest on secondary compilations (formal-conjectures PR, Wikipedia AI list); the AI-generated role holds regardless since Ji's independent AI reproduction says the same. The configuration is explicit and exactly verified, so it is a genuine counterexample in dimension 63, but the conjecture was already false since 1993, so it only moves a bound. Both surviving events are progress; per step 4 the AI role is the stronger, generated.

corrections.why: F3: the record itself says the dimension-63 construction 'improves a specific quantity (min. failing dimension) rather than resolving the general conjecture'; Borsuk's conjecture was already refuted in 1993 (Kahn-Kalai), so moving the smallest known counterexample dimension 64->63 is a bound, as is the R^4 upper bound 9->8. Neither settles the bullet's question on upper and lower bounds.
F14: progress rows carry direction null; also, a counterexample is never 'confirmed'.

other: kept. The object is an explicit exactly-verified configuration contradicting Borsuk's conjecture in R^63, but it is a bound on the counterexample dimension, not a counterexample to the (already refuted) bullet as a whole.
